newsitem.title: USA: U.S. agent shot while patrolling Mexican border.
newsitem.headline: U.S. agent shot while patrolling Mexican border.

text.p: A U.S. Border Patrol agent was shot and wounded early on Saturday while he was patrolling the border with Mexico, authorities said.
The incident took place at about 3 a.m. PDT (6 a.m. EDT/1000 GMT) near San Diego, where the agent was patrolling the San Ysidro section of the border.
An unidentified gunman fired at the agent's car from the Tijuana, Mexico, side of the border, U.S. Border Patrol spokesman Wayne Preston said.

Three shots were fired at the agent's marked vehicle, two of which pierced the car's windscreen. One bullet hit the agent in his left shoulder, while the second gave him a grazing head wound, Preston said.
The agent drove away from the scene, and minutes later was taken by ambulance to a local San Diego hospital where his condition was listed as stable.

Preston said there were no arrests made and the reason for the attack was unknown. The U.S. Border Patrol, the San Diego police, the FBI and the Mexican police were cooperating to investigate the incident, he said.
